name: Activated charcoal
mechanism: Adsorbs many toxins in GI tract reducing absorption
dosing: 50-100g orally for adults (single dose) — follow toxicology guidance
contraindications: Unprotected or compromised airway without airway protection; caustic ingestion (risk of aspiration and oesophageal injury); gastrointestinal perforation or obstruction
interactions: May adsorb orally administered antidotes or medications and reduce their effectiveness; consider route and timing before giving other oral therapies
monitoring: Ensure airway protection in patients with reduced consciousness; observe for vomiting and signs of aspiration; monitor clinical response and toxin-specific parameters
pregnancy: Use if indicated by toxicology advice; balance risks and benefits
sideEffects: Vomiting common; aspiration pneumonitis if airway not protected; may cause bowel obstruction with repeated doses in some cases
clinicalPearls: Most effective when given soon after ingestion (within 1 hour for many substances); consult toxicology centre for specific indications and dosing; single-dose activated charcoal is usual in most cases
indication: Selected cases of acute oral poisoning where the toxin is adsorbed by charcoal and airway is protected
